# Results — Study 700 (Bat-Harmonic)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Scott
Carney's **Bat** harmonic, which he calls the **most reliable** member of the harmonic-pattern
family: a five-point X-A-B-C-D structure where B retraces XA by 0.382-0.50 (a shallower pullback
than Gartley's 0.618), C retraces AB somewhere in 0.382-0.886, and **D retraces the ORIGINAL XA
leg by 0.886** — deep, but always staying *inside* the X-A range (unlike Butterfly/Crab, which
overshoot X). Believers expect a reversal the moment price touches D. Offline & deterministic
once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the
last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Basket: SPY, QQQ, AAPL,
MSFT, TSLA, NVDA — identical to siblings
[698-abcd-harmonic](../../698-abcd-harmonic/) and
[699-butterfly-harmonic](../../699-butterfly-harmonic/), for apples-to-apples comparison.*

## The protocol

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Pivot detection | percentage-threshold zigzag on daily closes, **pct = 2%**; a pivot is recorded only at its **confirmation bar** (never the earlier, still-unconfirmed extreme) |
| Bat arm — structural bands (both arms) | AB retraces XA by **0.382-0.50** (the Bat's characteristically shallow B); BC retraces AB by **0.382-0.886** (the shared XABCD band) |
| Bat arm — defining ratio | **D = A − 0.886 × (A − X)**, i.e. D retraces 0.886 of the *original* XA leg, always staying **inside** [X, A] |
| Placebo arm | identical structural pivots (same AB/BC bands), but each candidate's D-retracement *target* is drawn uniformly from [0.55, 1.20], kept ≥ 0.05 clear of 0.886 — "any deep retracement/extension zone near X", not specifically Carney's 0.886 |
| D-touch scan | forward window of **120 sessions** from C's confirmation bar; first bar whose high-low range brackets D (or closes within 0.75% of it) |
| Execution | enter the fade at the touch bar's **own close** (the touch is observed intrabar via that bar's high-low range — one documented convention, identical in both arms) |
| Base-rate control | ``n`` random entry days per ticker, matched to the **same empirical bullish/bearish mix** as the real Bat touches, pooled over **20 seeds** — neutralizes the equity-drift confound a directional rule inherits on an upward-drifting tape |
| Bonferroni | pooled headline + 6 per-ticker splits (5-day) = **7 tests**; critical \|*t*\| raised from 2.0 to **2.69** (family-wise α = 0.05, normal approximation) |
| Costs | one round trip = **2 × one-way cost × NAV**; net figures at 5 / 10 bps one-way |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC) *t* of the mean return against 0 (events can cluster in time); Welch *t* for the base-rate and placebo arm-vs-arm comparisons; Wilson interval on hit rate |

No survivorship: six large, currently-listed single names/ETFs, individually named — not a
membership-conditioned panel.

## The headline — Bat XABCD, forward returns at D

Pooled confirmed pivots: **6,055** → Bat XABCD candidates: **118** → D-touches: **89**.

| horizon | n | hit rate | mean (bps/event) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 89 | 51.7% | −12.41 | −0.46 |
| **5-day (headline)** | **89** | **40.4%** | **+7.58** | **+0.17** |
| 10-day | 89 | 44.9% | −36.93 | −0.48 |

Hit rate (5-day): **40.4%** (Wilson 95% [30.9%, 50.8%]) — the point estimate sits *below* a coin
flip. The headline mean is barely positive and nowhere close to *t* ≥ 2 at any horizon.

## Signal axis — Bat fade vs a random-day BASE RATE, Bonferroni-corrected

The base rate redraws, per ticker and pooled over 20 seeds, the same number of random entry days
with the same empirical bullish/bearish mix as the real Bat touches — the equity-drift confound a
directional rule inherits on an upward-drifting tape.

| horizon | Bat mean (bps) | base-rate mean (bps, n≈1,780) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | −12.41 | −11.32 | −0.04 |
| **5-day (headline)** | **+7.58** | −13.74 | **+0.45** |
| 10-day | −36.93 | +14.48 | −0.63 |

Per-ticker, 5-day, Bat vs its own matched-mix base rate:

| Ticker | Bat *n* | Bat mean (bps) | base-rate mean (bps) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 4  | +33.59  | −45.95 | +1.61 |
| QQQ  | 10 | −45.68  | −32.07 | −0.11 |
| AAPL | 19 | −119.46 | −8.70  | −1.54 |
| MSFT | 15 | +100.13 | −28.61 | +1.36 |
| TSLA | 14 | +202.77 | −34.00 | +1.73 |
| NVDA | 27 | −39.77  | +13.05 | −0.50 |

**Bonferroni correction across 7 tests** (pooled headline + 6 per-ticker splits, 5-day): critical
|*t*| = **2.69** (family-wise α = 0.05, normal approximation).

- **0 of 7 tests clear even the uncorrected |*t*| ≥ 2 bar.** TSLA's drift-matched comparison
  (Welch *t* = +1.73) is the closest — and it still falls short before any multiple-comparison
  penalty is applied.
- **0 of 7 survive Bonferroni.** There is no honest reading of this basket in which the Bat's
  D-touch fade beats a directionally-matched coin flip.

## Tradability axis — the fade timer, net of costs

One round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV per event.

| hold | gross mean (bps) | net @ 5 bps (bps) | net @ 10 bps (bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | −12.41 (t=−0.46) | −22.41 (t=−0.84) | −32.41 (t=−1.21) |
| 3-day  | +2.50 (t=+0.07)  | −7.50 (t=−0.20)  | −17.50 (t=−0.47) |
| **5-day** | **+7.58 (t=+0.17)** | **−2.42 (t=−0.05)** | **−12.42 (t=−0.27)** |
| 10-day | −36.93 (t=−0.48) | −46.93 (t=−0.61) | −56.93 (t=−0.74) |
| 20-day | −143.17 (t=−1.07) | −153.17 (t=−1.14) | −163.17 (t=−1.22) |

No hold length produces a gross mean that is both positive *and* statistically distinguishable
from zero, and the best gross case (5-day, +7.58 bps) flips negative the moment a single 5 bps
one-way cost is charged. Longer holds get worse, not better — the 20-day fade loses **143 bps
gross** on average.

## Third axis (myth-check) — does the specific 0.886 ratio beat a placebo retracement/extension zone?

Identical pivots and structural AB/BC bands; only the D-retracement *target* differs (Bat: fixed
0.886; placebo: drawn per-candidate from [0.55, 1.20], excluding a ±0.05 band around 0.886).

| horizon | Bat mean (bps) | placebo mean (bps) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | −12.41 | −14.45 | +0.05 |
| **5-day (headline)** | **+7.58** | −7.64 | **+0.22** |
| 10-day | −36.93 | −23.22 | −0.12 |

Placebo candidates: 118 → placebo D-touches: 92.

Per-instrument, 5-day, Bat vs placebo:

| Ticker | Bat mean (bps) | placebo mean (bps) | beats placebo? |
|---|--:|--:|:--:|
| SPY  | +33.59  | −66.06  | **yes** |
| QQQ  | −45.68  | +114.72 | no |
| AAPL | −119.46 | −79.11  | no |
| MSFT | +100.13 | +125.90 | no |
| TSLA | +202.77 | −86.09  | **yes** |
| NVDA | −39.77  | −36.99  | no |

Bat beats the placebo on **2 of 6** tickers. At the pooled headline horizon the Welch *t* is a
negligible +0.22 — Carney's specific 0.886 ratio shows no detectable edge over an arbitrary
deep-retracement/extension zone built from the identical pivot geometry.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic mean-reverting price index (tunable `mean_rev` knob toward a slow EMA), pooled
across a **synthetic 6-name basket per seed** (mirrors the real pooled sample size); no network.

| world | *n* (pooled) | mean (bps/event) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (`mean_rev = 0`), **20 seeds** | ~85/seed | — | mean **−0.12** (sd 1.24), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 2/20 seeds** |
| planted `mean_rev = 0.12` (seed 700) | 84 | +126.21 | **+5.18** |

The null fires close to (a touch above) the nominal ~5% false-positive rate expected of a *t* ≥ 2
threshold over 20 independent draws — unsurprising given the small per-seed sample (~85 pooled
touches); a planted mean-reversion tendency lights up sharply. The pipeline can find a real
Bat-shaped reversal effect when one is actually there — the flat real-tape result above is the
genuine article, not a broken detector. *(A faithful-engine / power check only; never cited in
support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The Bat's 5-day fade-at-D return is **+7.58 bps/event, HAC *t* = +0.17** —
  essentially zero, with a hit rate (40.4%) *below* a coin flip. Against the drift-matched base
  rate the pooled Welch *t* is +0.45, and **0 of 7 Bonferroni-corrected tests** (pooled + 6
  per-ticker, critical |*t*| = 2.69) survive. TSLA's individually notable cell (gross *t* = +2.34,
  vs-base-rate *t* = +1.73) is the closest call on the board and still falls short before any
  multiple-comparison penalty.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No hold length (1/3/5/10/20 days) clears *t* ≥ 2 on the positive
  side, the best gross case (+7.58 bps, 5-day) turns negative at a single 5 bps one-way cost, and
  longer holds bleed more (20-day: −143 bps gross).
- **"Beats a placebo retracement/extension zone (i.e. is 0.886 the 'most reliable' ratio, as
  Carney claims)?" — BUSTED.** The Bat arm beats its own placebo control on only 2 of 6 tickers,
  and the pooled 5-day Welch *t* (+0.22) shows no detectable specificity for 0.886 over an
  arbitrary deep zone built from the identical pivots — consistent with sibling
  [698-abcd-harmonic](../../698-abcd-harmonic/)'s finding that Fibonacci ratio labels add nothing
  over a randomized control on the same six tapes.
